name: The Yardbirds
hook: A London blues band that went through Eric Clapton, Jeff Beck and Jimmy Page in five years, and turned into Led Zeppelin.
blurb: The Yardbirds formed in southwest London in 1963 out of the Metropolitan Blues Quartet. Their manager, Giorgio Gomelsky, made them the house band at the Crawdaddy Club in Richmond after the Rolling Stones, and set up tours backing the American blues singer Sonny Boy Williamson in 1963 and 1964. Three famous guitarists passed through: Eric Clapton, who left in March 1965 because the band was going pop with 'For Your Love'; Jeff Beck (1965 to 1966), who experimented with fuzz and feedback; and Jimmy Page (1966 to 1968), who played his guitar with a bow. On their first American tour they recorded 'Train Kept A-Rollin'' in Memphis in September 1965, with Sam Phillips engineering. In 1968 Page's version of the band toured Scandinavia as the New Yardbirds, and that October became Led Zeppelin.
